summary.headline: Crompton Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18.2% YoY to Rs 2,263 Cr and EBITDA 24.1% to Rs 205 Cr, with margin up 40 bps to 9%.
summary.overview: Crompton delivered its third straight quarter of double-digit revenue growth, with all business segments growing double digits per management. Revenue rose 18.2% YoY to Rs 2,263 Cr and EBITDA rose 24.1% YoY to Rs 205 Cr at a 9% margin. PBT excluding exceptional items grew 36.2%; the prior-year quarter carried a Rs 20 Cr Baroda plant restructuring exceptional, which inflates reported PAT growth of 65%. Management said price increases of about 80% of cost inflation have been passed through, supply disruptions from Q1 are over, and inventory days are back to year-ago levels. E-commerce was subdued due to a channel repositioning, and A&P spend was lower in H1.

financial_highlights.metric: Exceptional item (prior year, Baroda plant restructuring)

financial_highlights.change: Historical run-rate Rs 250-260 Cr per year

segments.name: ECD (Electrical Consumer Durables: fans, pumps, appliances)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 19.4% YoY with EBIT margin up YoY to 11.6%; BLDC fans grew about 40% in general trade. SDA grew over 20%, and LDA grew at double digits led by water heaters.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 298 Cr, up 14.3% YoY, driven by B2C ceiling and outdoor lights and B2B industrial and indoor commercial. EBIT margin 12.9%, lower YoY due to pre-contracted B2B orders.

segments.name: Butterfly
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 15.9% YoY excluding an in-house mixer grinder sale in the base; growth was largely price-led. Management said the core business grew about 16%.

segments.name: Solar pumps
segments.commentary: Slowed as Kusum 1.1 order inflow tapered; management expects a pickup after Kusum 2.0 is announced. More than 50% of the AP government order book has been executed.

segments.name: Solar rooftop and wires
segments.commentary: Solar rooftop (B2C and C&I) is live in six to seven states; wires launched in South India in Q1 and extended to Punjab, Delhi NCR and Gujarat. Management described both as nascent.

segments.name: LKA and Rhion
segments.commentary: Restructured under Butterfly CBO Shweta Sagar, to leverage the Butterfly ecosystem. Management cited a prior EBITDA loss of Rs 16-25 Cr for the business.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Grew more than 70% YoY to a record quarterly revenue, led by fans with pumps, LDA and SDA also exported; markets are Africa, Middle East and South Asia. Margins are slightly lower than domestic, but sales are on cash terms.

guidance_outlook: Management says the company is on track for its medium-term guidance and expects double-digit revenue and profit growth to continue over the coming quarters.
Long-term EBITDA margin ambition of 11-12% by FY29, as stated in the investor deck; management said this is on a larger revenue base.
New businesses are targeted at 14-15% of revenue in the long run; they were about 10% of revenue in Q2 FY27 per the call.
Solar rooftop order execution is expected to complete in the next quarter, with some spillover after that.
A&P spend is expected to stay broadly at last year's absolute level, subject to macro conditions.
Fans are targeted at 1.5-1.7x category growth, per the investor day.
capex_capacity: Evaluation of a greenfield manufacturing plant is at an advanced stage, to add capacity in fans, appliances and wires.
Pumps and most new businesses (solar pumps, solar rooftop, wires, LKA) are outsourced; the company has not yet committed to in-house manufacturing.
Management said there is no supply constraint today.
Solar rooftop installation is done through an agency partner on the company's behalf.
New businesses leverage existing go-to-market and supply chain, so no separate sales teams or fresh cost centres are planned.
demand_pricing: Cumulative price increases of 11-15% across most non-lighting businesses over the last six months, and about 15-16% in some; fans cumulatively about 17-18% over nine months.
About 80% of cost inflation has been passed through; the remainder is being covered by Unnati cost savings and operating leverage.
Q2 was the first quarter in which price increases were largely passed on with positive volume growth across categories, per management.
General trade (about 80% of business) and rural both grew double digits; e-commerce was subdued after a deliberate channel repositioning.
Competitors have announced price increases, but management said these have not always been implemented.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been passed on, and what more is needed for Q3 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price increases were 11-15% across businesses excluding lighting, and about 80% of cost increases have been passed on. Further increases will follow as commodities move.

qa_highlights.question: How much solar rooftop revenue was recognised in Q1, and how much of the order remains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a percentage split. About half the order has been executed across Q1 and Q2; most of the remainder is expected to complete next quarter, with some spillover.

qa_highlights.question: Why is fan pricing lower than the overall price-hike number?
qa_highlights.answer: The company said the 15% figure refers to cumulative price increases over the last two quarters, with fans at the top of the range. Fans cumulatively rose about 17-18% over nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Solar rooftop margin structure: is installation cost borne by Crompton?
qa_highlights.answer: Crompton sells a turnkey product at about Rs 1.8 lakh for a 3 kW unit, with installation included. An agency partner performs the installation on Crompton's behalf, so the cost sits between gross margin and EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why did A&P spend fall as a share of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower e-commerce promotion spend from channel repositioning, and brand relaunch costs booked outside A&P. H1 A&P was about Rs 100 Cr against a Rs 250-260 Cr annual run-rate.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA margin ambition of 11-12% by FY29 a margin recovery or expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 11-12% is a recovery to the FY25 level of 11.8%, with operating leverage coming on a higher revenue base as growth is raised about 2.5x from the phase-one average of about 6%.

risks_watch: Commodity cost volatility and geopolitics; about 20% of cost inflation is still unrecovered.
Solar pump order inflow remains lumpy until Kusum 2.0 orders come through.
Lighting B2B margin pressure from pre-contracted orders.
E-commerce revenue remains subdued during the channel repositioning.
A&P comparability and the classification of brand relaunch spend outside A&P.
Solar rooftop profitability depends on the agency installation model and selective government tendering.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and brand, but cautious on commodity costs, which management said are unpredictable. Management was evasive on fan volume drivers and on specific solar rooftop revenue recognition, and gave no quantified margin guidance beyond the FY29 ambition.
key_quotes: This is the third quarter of double-digit revenue growth and is accompanied by excellent profit growth.
Solar rooftops by themselves are Rs.26,000 crore business.
Exports grew at more than 70% this quarter and recorded the highest ever quarterly revenues.

adds.what: Greenfield manufacturing plant for fans, appliances and wires (evaluation at advanced stage, no capacity size or timing given)

growth.why: Management says it is on track for double-digit revenue and profit growth to continue and holds 11-12% EBITDA margin by FY29, backed by about 80% cost pass-through, positive volume growth and a greenfield plant still at evaluation stage with no size or timing given.
